biography: Kejun Ying is an incoming assistant professor. He will start his own lab in the Bay Area in January 2027; the exact institution will be announced later. He is currently a postdoctoral fellow at Stanford University in Tony Wyss-Coray’s lab and at the University of Washington in David Baker’s lab, supported by an NIH/NIA F99K00 fellowship. He received the 2026 WAIC Yunfan Award.

His research focuses on AI for Science, with an emphasis on AI for Biology and AI for Aging. He develops foundation models and world models for biological data, and builds agentic systems. His work includes biological age modeling and aging intervention discovery, brain aging and neurodegeneration, systematic analyses of cancer and age-related diseases, and de novo protein design for aging interventions. His previous work includes a causal inference-based aging clock, ClockBase, and MethylGPT.

Hello! I'm Kejun Albert Ying, an incoming assistant professor. I will start my own lab in the Bay Area in January 2027. The exact institution will be announced later.

I am now a postdoctoral fellow at Stanford University in Tony Wyss-Coray's lab and at the University of Washington in David Baker's lab, supported by an NIH/NIA F99K00 fellowship. I earned my Ph.D. in Biological Sciences from Harvard Medical School (2025) in Vadim Gladyshev's lab and an M.Sc. in Computational Science and Engineering from Harvard SEAS (2024), and I received the 2026 WAIC Yunfan Award.

My research focuses on AI for Science, with an emphasis on AI for Biology and AI for Aging. I develop foundation models and world models for biological data, and build agentic systems. I model biological age and discover aging interventions, study brain aging and neurodegeneration, analyze cancer and age-related diseases systematically, and design de novo proteins for aging interventions.

AI-Driven Discovery
ClockBase Agent
An autonomous AI system that mines large-scale molecular profiles to discover aging interventions. ClockBase Agent reanalyzed 43,602 intervention-control comparisons across multiple aging biomarkers, identifying 500+ compounds that significantly reduce biological age. Featured on MIT Technology Review.
Ying, K., Tyshkovskiy, A., Moldakozhayev, A.,..., Wyss-Coray, T., & Gladyshev, V. N. (2025). Autonomous AI Agents Discover Aging Interventions from Millions of Molecular Profiles. bioRxiv. doi:10.1101/2023.02.28.530532

blocks.authors: K Ying, H Liu, AE Tarkhov,..., VN Gladyshev

blocks.text: Causal Inference for Epigenetic Ageing
blocks.description: A perspective on applying causal inference methods to understand the relationship between epigenetic changes and the aging process.

blocks.text: MethylGPT: A Foundation Model for the DNA Methylome

spans.text: MethylGPT: A Foundation Model for the DNA Methylome

blocks.authors: K Ying, J Song, H Cui, Y Zhang,..., VN Gladyshev
blocks.description: MethylGPT learns the grammar of the human DNA methylome, how CpG sites are methylated together, without labels from 169,010 public methylation profiles. One model then reads any of four array platforms and carries what it learned into imputation, age, sex, tissue and aging-clock outputs.
